summary.text: Specializing to \(p=3\) and \(r=2\), direct evaluation of the finite binomial sums gives \(a(9)-a(3)=2343591352008=3^9\cdot119066776\), with the cofactor not divisible by \(3\), so the difference is not divisible by the formal statement’s modulus \(3^{12}\). Thus this refutes only the inadvertently strengthened formal modulus \(p^3p^rp^{2r}p^3=p^{3r+6}\); at this example the stated conjectural modulus \(p^{3r+3}=3^9\) does divide the difference.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
 A(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom nk^2\binom{n+k}{k}^2,
 \qquad
 C(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom nk^2\binom{n+k}{k},
\]
and define the sequence in question by
\[
 a(n)=5A(n)+14C(n-1)\qquad(n\geq 1).
\]

There is an important distinction between the stated OEIS conjecture and the precise universally quantified assertion that was accepted and disproved. The OEIS conjecture asks for congruence modulo
\[
p^{3r+3}.
\]
The accepted formal assertion instead asks for congruence modulo
\[
p^3\,p^r\,p^{2r}\,p^3=p^{3+r+2r+3}=p^{3r+6}.
\]
The following is a complete disproof of that latter assertion. At the end, we explain why it does not disprove the OEIS modulus as canonically stated.

Take
\[
p=3,\qquad r=2.
\]
These values satisfy every side condition: 3 is prime, \(3\geq 3\), and \(2\geq 2\). The proposed universal congruence would therefore imply
\[
a(3^2)\equiv a(3^{2-1})
 \pmod{3^3\,3^2\,3^{2\cdot2}\,3^3},
\]
that is,
\[
a(9)\equiv a(3)\pmod{3^{12}}.
\]
We now evaluate both sequence values directly from their defining finite sums.

First, for \(A(3)\), the four summands
\(\binom 3k^2\binom{3+k}{k}^2\), for \(k=0,1,2,3\), are respectively
\[
1,\,144,\,900,\,400.
\]
Consequently
\[
A(3)=1+144+900+400=1445.
\]
For \(C(2)\), the three summands
\(\binom 2k^2\binom{2+k}{k}\), for \(k=0,1,2\), are
\[
1,\,12,\,6,
\]
so
\[
C(2)=1+12+6=19.
\]
It follows that
\[
a(3)=5A(3)+14C(2)=5\cdot1445+14\cdot19=7225+266=7491.
\]

For \(A(9)\), the ten summands
\(\binom 9k^2\binom{9+k}{k}^2\), indexed by \(k=0,1,\ldots,9\), are
\[
\begin{array}{c|r}
k&\binom 9k^2\binom{9+k}{k}^2\\ \hline
0&1\\
1&8{,}100\\
2&3{,}920{,}400\\
3&341{,}510{,}400\\
4&8{,}116{,}208{,}100\\
5&63{,}631{,}071{,}504\\
6&176{,}752{,}976{,}400\\
7&169{,}612{,}185{,}600\\
8&47{,}869{,}064{,}100\\
9&2{,}363{,}904{,}400.
\end{array}
\]
Their sum is
\[
A(9)=468{,}690{,}849{,}005.
\]

The value needed in the second part of \(a(9)\) is \(C(8)\). Its nine summands
\(\binom 8k^2\binom{8+k}{k}\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots,8\), are
\[
\begin{array}{c|r}
k&\binom 8k^2\binom{8+k}{k}\\ \hline
0&1\\
1&576\\
2&35{,}280\\
3&517{,}440\\
4&2{,}425{,}500\\
5&4{,}036{,}032\\
6&2{,}354{,}352\\
7&411{,}840\\
8&12{,}870.
\end{array}
\]
Thus
\[
C(8)=9{,}793{,}891.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(9)
 &=5A(9)+14C(8)\\
 &=5\cdot468{,}690{,}849{,}005
   +14\cdot9{,}793{,}891\\
 &=2{,}343{,}591{,}359{,}499.
\end{aligned}
\]

Subtracting gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(9)-a(3)
 &=2{,}343{,}591{,}359{,}499-7{,}491\\
 &=2{,}343{,}591{,}352{,}008.
\end{aligned}
\]
This difference factors as
\[
2{,}343{,}591{,}352{,}008
 =3^9\cdot119{,}066{,}776
 =2^3\cdot3^9\cdot17\cdot875{,}491.
\]
The factor \(119{,}066{,}776\) is not divisible by 3: its decimal digit sum is
\[
1+1+9+0+6+6+7+7+6=43,
\]
which is not divisible by 3. Hence the exact exponent of 3 dividing \(a(9)-a(3)\) is 9. In particular, \(3^{12}\) does not divide the difference. Equivalently, since
\[
3^{12}=531{,}441,
\]
one can write
\[
a(9)-a(3)
 =531{,}441\cdot4{,}409{,}880+314{,}928,
\]
with nonzero remainder \(314{,}928\). Therefore
\[
a(9)\not\equiv a(3)\pmod{3^{12}}.
\]
This contradicts the instance \(p=3,r=2\) of the accepted universal assertion, and so that assertion is false.

Finally, this calculation also pinpoints the mismatch with the canonical OEIS conjecture. For \(p=3,r=2\), the canonical modulus is only
\[
p^{3r+3}=3^{3\cdot2+3}=3^9.
\]
The displayed factorization shows that \(3^9\) does divide \(a(9)-a(3)\). Thus the witness \((p,r)=(3,2)\) satisfies, rather than violates, the canonical congruence modulo \(p^{3r+3}\). Accordingly, the argument is a disproof of the stronger, accepted formal statement with modulus \(p^3p^rp^{2r}p^3=p^{3r+6}\); it is not a disproof of the canonical OEIS conjecture with modulus \(p^{3r+3}\).
